historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR (14.0%) diverges far more than 30% from revenue 3-yr CAGR (2.1%). Book equity is a poor anchor here: it is ~4bn against ~85bn of market value and is driven by buybacks and treasury-stock retirement rather than retained earnings. The 5-yr equity CAGR (5.0%) happens to agree with 5-yr revenue (5.1%), and that is the figure used.
historical_growth.notes: FY2020/FY2022 to FY2025, annual rows. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less cash-flow SBC; SBC is only ~0.5% of sales so owner and reported CAGRs differ by under 0.5pp). The FCF series is dominated by working-capital swings: FY2020 was a pandemic working-capital release (3.0bn owner FCF), FY2022 an inventory rebuild plus HQ capex (1.2bn), so neither endpoint CAGR means much. Revenue FY2015-FY2025 compounds at 7.6% including Valspar (2017); ex-Valspar roughly 5%.

scenario_narratives.base: Management's own framing holds: demand stays soft into 2027 (Y1 growth 4%, organic only now that Suvinil has anniversaried), then existing-home turnover and repaint demand recover at a normal pace. Paint Stores keeps adding ~2% to the store base each year and takes price in low single digits, giving ~5-5.5% growth in the middle years before fading to 3.5%. Adjusted EBITDA margin rises from 19.5% to 21% by year 6 as volume returns to a largely fixed store and sales-rep cost base, the ~75m of 2027 cost savings land, and Suvinil's dilution of Consumer Brands margin is worked off. Capex settles near 2.3% of sales with the HQ build finished. Gordon growth binds the terminal value (18.7x) rather than the 20x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: The housing cycle turns earlier and harder -- mortgage rates fall, existing-home sales normalise from 2027 -- and Sherwin converts the structural share opening left by PPG's exit from US/Canada architectural retail and the closure of regional chains such as Kelly-Moore. Growth runs 6.5-7% for four years and volume leverage through the store network, plus Latin American scale from Suvinil, lifts Adjusted EBITDA margin to 23%, above anything the company has reported. This needs both the cycle and the share gain to arrive, which is why it carries less than the default bull weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: Softer-for-longer turns out to be the new level, not a pause: high mortgage rates lock owners in place, DIY and Consumer Brands stay structurally weak, and tariff-driven resin, TiO2 and packaging inflation outruns pricing as the Q3-2026 gross-margin compression (-140bp) persists. Growth is 2-3.5% (store openings and price only) and margin slips to 18.5% as SG&A from new stores and sales reps is not absorbed. Leverage, already at the top of the 2.0-2.5x target after debt-funded buybacks and the HQ, leaves less room to keep shrinking the share count. An adverse lead-pigment or environmental ruling would come on top of this and is not in the numbers. The terminal value does not hit the zero floor; the business remains strongly cash generative on this path.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Sherwin-Williams is a high-quality, moderately cyclical compounder valued on unlevered owner free cash flow built from components off the last twelve months, with SBC (small, ~0.65% of sales including an upper-bound allowance for equity-award withholding) fully expensed and the share count held flat. House and street values sit close together because SBC is small; the gap between value and price here is about the discount rate and the terminal multiple the market grants a dominant franchise, not about accounting regime. The debt-funded buyback is treated as value-neutral, so per-share growth from a shrinking count is deliberately not credited.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal-value dominated: the result is highly sensitive to WACC and terminal growth; the market price implies a required return well below the 8.5% used here
The margin path (19.5% to 21% base) depends on a housing-turnover recovery that management does not expect before 2028
Net debt of 12.3bn (2.5x Adjusted EBITDA) includes 2.35bn of short-term borrowings and 1.5bn of long-term debt maturing within a year, to be refinanced at higher coupons
Lead pigment / lead-based paint litigation and the Texas AG environmental suit are unaccrued and excluded from the equity bridge
Equity-award tax allowance is an upper bound and finance lease liabilities are excluded from net debt; the two roughly offset (each about 1-3/share)
Buybacks of ~2.5bn/yr exceed free cash flow after dividends; a model that credited the shrinking share count would read higher, one that charged the incremental debt would not

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 289.86-377.77
data_sources.financials: SHW_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL); Q3-2026 10-Q (balance sheet, cash flow, share count, EBITDA reconciliation, real estate financing note) and FY2025 10-K (EBITDA reconciliation, cash flow, lease note, contractual obligations) in research/SHW/Extracted/
data_sources.qualitative: SHW_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): FY2026 guidance as of Q3-2026 results, 27 Oct 2026

inputs.share_count_basis: 241.588m shares outstanding on the Q3-2026 10-Q cover (30 Sep 2026) plus 2.1m dilutive securities (Q3-2026 diluted weighted average 242.8m less basic 240.7m). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow add-back, LTM to 30 Sep 2026: FY2025 10-K 123.5 less 9M-2025 91.5 plus 9M-2026 85.0 = 117.0. No combined figure or separate net-settlement tax line is published; 48.9 added = treasury-stock column of 'Stock-based compensation activity' in the 9M-2026 equity statement (shares delivered for option exercise price and/or tax withholding). That is an UPPER BOUND on equity-award taxes because it includes exercise-price deliveries.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rates. Cost of equity ~9.4% (10-yr UST ~4.3% + beta ~1.05 x ~4.8% ERP); after-tax cost of debt ~4.0% (blended coupon ~5.1% x (1 - 23%)); debt ~13% of capital at market (12.6bn debt vs ~85bn market cap) gives ~8.7%; 8.5% used. One WACC across all three scenarios: risk is charged in the scenario weights, not again in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: the ~592m/yr operating lease cost (FY2025 10-K lease note) is rent expense INSIDE Adjusted EBITDA, so the 2,186.7m of operating lease liabilities is NOT in net debt and lease_cost_pct_path is zero. The 817.9m real-estate-financing liability (failed sale-leaseback of the new global HQ; its cost runs through interest expense, not EBITDA) IS included in total_debt. Finance lease liabilities (undiscounted payments 648.7m, 600.7m of it beyond five years) are not included; the discounted amount is not broken out in the 10-Q and is worth roughly 1/share.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon -- standard operating company (paint and coatings manufacturer-retailer), not a bank/REIT/holdco. FRESH BUILD, no prior valuation. BASE PERIOD is the LTM to 30 Sep 2026, not FY2025, so the flows start where the balance sheet stops: Y1 = Oct-2026 to Sep-2027. Using FY2025 as FY0 against a Sep-2026 balance sheet would count nine months of cash twice (it has already been spent on 2.36bn of buybacks that reduced the share count). LTM revenue 24,912.1 = FY2025 23,574.3 - 9M-2025 17,978.4 + 9M-2026 19,316.2. LTM Adjusted EBITDA 4,853.3 (19.5%) = 4,608.9 - 3,615.8 + 3,860.2, management definition; it is AFTER the ~118m/yr amortization of non-traded (tax-credit) investments, which is why the ~23% effective rate, already net of those credits, is the right tax rate to pair with it. LTM D&A 747.1 (depreciation 394.3, intangible amortization 352.8, of which ~265m is Valspar and rolls off). LTM capex 605.8 (2.4%), down from 1,070 in FY2024 as the HQ/R&D build completed; management guides core capex ~2% of sales. NET DEBT 12,348.8 = long-term debt incl. current portion 9,441.5 + short-term borrowings 2,353.6 + real estate financing 817.9 - cash 264.2; 2.5x LTM Adjusted EBITDA, at the top of the company's 2.0-2.5x target. INTEREST INCOME not stripped: the company is a net debtor (17m of interest income on 264m of cash). reported_fcf is the levered figure (operating cash 3,683.6 less capex 605.8); the projections are unlevered, so Y1 FCF is not directly comparable to last_fcf -- add back ~415m of after-tax interest. WORKING CAPITAL: receivables + inventories - payables were 2,755m at Dec-2025 (11.7% of sales), so growth consumes cash; wc_capture is -10%. BUYBACKS: 2,475m repurchased in the LTM against 166m of SBC cost -- the flat count is funded many times over and the count is actually shrinking ~2.5%/yr, partly debt-financed; that shrink is not credited (buybacks at market are value-neutral here). NOT IN THE BRIDGE: lead pigment / lead-based paint litigation (unaccrued, no estimable range) and the Texas AG Garland suit -- carried in the bear weight instead. Price is a regular Friday close, not an after-hours print.

bear.narrative: Mortgage rates stay high, existing-home turnover never recovers to pre-2022 levels, and raw-material inflation outruns pricing; margin settles at 18.5%.

base.narrative: Softer-for-longer through 2027, then a normal housing-turnover recovery; organic growth ~5% mid-cycle (2% store count + price + share), margin to 21% on volume leverage.

bull.narrative: Housing turnover normalises from 2027 and Sherwin takes the share PPG and regional chains vacated; margin to 23%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): leverage sits at the top of management's own target band while interest expense is rising, management itself now guides weak demand into 2027, and the unaccrued lead-pigment litigation is a tail the flows do not carry. Base 50%: it is management's stated outlook followed by an ordinary cyclical recovery in a business with a long record of steady share gain. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs two independent things -- an early housing recovery and margins above the historical peak.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
